overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation on the alleged points: the Feb. 27 minutes were timely approved, the website-posting claim was declined as not a violation, and the Sept. 23 community forum was not a meeting because members did not deliberate.

allegations.summary: Subcommittee's February 27 meeting minutes were allegedly not timely approved.
allegations.key_passage: Because the Subcommittee had not met more than three times after February 27, and the Committee approved the Subcommittee’s minutes promptly after disbanding the Subcommittee, we find that the Subcommittee’s February 27 meeting minutes were timely approved.

allegations.summary: Committee and Subcommittee allegedly did not post meeting minutes to the Town's website.
allegations.key_passage: Because this allegation, even if true, would not violate the Open Meeting Law, we decline to review it.

allegations.summary: Committee allegedly convened a September 23 meeting (community forum) without posting notice.
allegations.key_passage: Because the community forum did not include any deliberation by members of the Committee, it was not a “meeting” for purposes of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Committee allegedly failed to create minutes for the September 23 community forum.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, the Committee was not required to post notice for the community forum or create minutes.

allegations.summary: Committee or Subcommittee allegedly convened additional meetings without posting notice or creating minutes.
allegations.key_passage: We find no evidence that either the Committee or Subcommittee violated the Open Meeting Law by convening additional meetings without posting notice or creating minutes.
